turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes, and I'd like to start with why my son found out about a zero from his phone in the middle of class. Who decided that, and when?
You're welcome. Now answer the question: who decided, and when?
Let me show you the version history. The document was created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, and 1,406 words arrived in two pastes six minutes apart.

Turn the screen, I'll read it myself. 11:31, two pastes, six minutes apart, I'm writing that down. "Created" only tells me when that file was opened, not where the words were written, and you still haven't told me who entered the zero before anyone called me.
Can you summarize what we've agreed so far in bullet points?
Put it in an email yourself. We've agreed nothing; my position is the zero comes off and you tell me who entered it without calling home.
Just a quick numbered list is fine.
No lists, Hale, I'm not your secretary. Procedure 4.2 says you call the parent before any mark goes in, and the zero went in on November 3 with no call. Who entered it?
